failedLinuxAttempts.assessment: Rosetta readlinkat /proc assertion interrupted the intentional-failure setup fixture before its deliberate failure. No source change, watchdog timeout or forced cleanup.

The full fixed-source run exhausted the 240-second lifecycle-job budget under amd64 emulation. The watchdog forced cleanup and still observed one process at its final sample; the stopped container retained an owned profile. Its removal released that writable layer. This failed run is not a conformance pass; watchdog cleanup and the final full Linux matrix remain open.

All preceding 26 groups passed, but storage collection failed when Chromium cancelled a prior-document interception during origin traversal. Production now consumes only the exact stale-interception rejection without replay; unrelated failures still propagate. Two protocol-level unit cases and repeated real multi-origin snapshots cover the fix.

initialFailures: Linux attempt 028 caught Invalid InterceptionId during a successor-origin snapshot. The production interceptor now consumes that exact native cancellation rejection without replay while preserving every unrelated protocol failure; no blanket catch was introduced.
TypeScript required explicit canonical-cookie field narrowing; the fixed package build passed.
The initial child-origin fixture called Frame.evaluate, which is not in the implemented slice; the fixture now uses a supported child-frame locator after the child script reads its storage.
An unsafe-port navigation did not fail because interception fulfilled it. The restoration rollback case now uses a native invalid cookie rejection and asserts acknowledged resource disposal.
Rust clippy required the test module to follow implementation items; the module was moved without changing behavior.

The worker fixture exposed a pinned-reference side effect: fallback storage collection ran a service-worker-supplied document and mutated storage. It is preserved as a separate observed difference in SPECS S4.j, not erased from differential claims.
The initial cookie sort used JSON property order, which differs between the reference and Rust. Sorting now uses explicit cookie identity fields; complete cookie payloads remain compared.
The strengthened rollback fixture initially read error.cleanup instead of the public error.details.cleanup. Correcting that access verified the resourceDisposed acknowledgement.
tests: Two deterministic connection-level cases prove cancelled interception does not replay or fail a successor and unrelated errors remain visible
Six repeated multi-origin snapshots per browser corpus cover prior-document subresource cancellation
Native cookie attributes, expiry, replacement, URL/domain/path filtering, regex deletion and partitioned cookies
Cookie-only state restoration with partition metadata and no public page
Exact UTF-16 localStorage values and keys including lone surrogates, NUL, astral text and special property names
HTTP and HTTPS origin restoration without backend requests
Real HTTP Set-Cookie login authenticated after object/file restoration before page startup
Closed-page and same-process child origins, empty-origin omission and sessionStorage exclusion
Bounded collection, preserved prior state file after failure and recovery of the existing page
Native batch rejection before partial cookie application and failed-context rollback
Stopped-browser cookie read deadline, context-close interruption and uncertain-mutation owner retirement
Runner context-option inheritance, explicit state override and state-file fixture
